bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Group structure is a holding-plus-operating hybrid: Ethos Limited 50.11% ("Together with our WOS", retails premium and luxury watches, listed on BSE and NSE through an IPO in 2022), Mahen Distribution Limited 100% WOS, Estima AG 100% WOS, Pylania SA 100% WOS, Kamla Int. Holdings SA 100% WOS (an SPV and holding company), Silvercity Brands AG 93.08% directly and indirectly through subsidiaries (Favre Leuba), and Artisan Watch Products Pvt. Ltd. 80% held through KDDL Ltd.
- Standalone balance sheet at Mar'26: Equity Rs 383.9 Cr (Mar'25 Rs 331.4 Cr), non-current borrowings Rs 62.0 Cr, current borrowings Rs 48.0 Cr, non-current investments Rs 186.6 Cr, cash and cash equivalents Rs 13.8 Cr, inventories Rs 77.2 Cr and trade receivables Rs 103.3 Cr on total assets of Rs 625.0 Cr.
- Consolidated balance sheet at Mar'26: Equity Rs 1,917.9 Cr, of which Non Controlling Interest is Rs 837.6 Cr (Mar'25 Rs 495.5 Cr); non-current borrowings Rs 73.9 Cr and current borrowings Rs 82.6 Cr, against cash and cash equivalents Rs 208.5 Cr and bank balances Rs 526.5 Cr, on total assets of Rs 2,754.8 Cr.
- Subsidiary monetisation and upstreaming have been a recurring source of standalone profit: FY24 other income of Rs 193.8 Cr is footnoted as "Stake sale in Ethos in the open market worth Rs 121.7 cr and Rs 72.1 cr interim dividend received from Mahen Distribution Limited"; FY23 other income of Rs 49.7 Cr is footnoted "Exceptional income – OFS/Brand Sale"; FY26 other income of Rs 18.0 Cr is "Dividend Income received from Mahen Distribution Ltd".
- Working capital is inventory-heavy at group level: consolidated inventories rose to Rs 792.8 Cr at Mar'26 from Rs 657.9 Cr (Mar'25), Rs 489.8 Cr (Mar'24), Rs 381.0 Cr (Mar'23) and Rs 279.5 Cr (Mar'22); consolidated lease liabilities stand at Rs 286.9 Cr non-current plus Rs 68.4 Cr current.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Long-standing customer relationships, especially with partners in the Swiss watch industry, described by the Company as a major strength on the export front
- Presence across both manufacturing and retail, enabling participation across the luxury value chain with a diversified business portfolio
- Eigen focuses on chosen segments requiring high complexity, skills and capabilities along with high entry barriers, and has moved from component supplier to strategic solution provider for global technology leaders
- Manufacturing setup equipped to handle complex export requirements, with design capabilities, fast development cycles, shortened response times and competitive pricing
- Consistent emphasis on product quality, operational agility and reliability in quality and delivery, which the Company links to tangible market share gains
- Eigen's expertise in progressive tool design and die-making, delivering high-speed, zero-defect production for complex assemblies
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Sustained slowdown in the Swiss watch industry, the Company's core export end-market — Swiss watch exports declined 1.7% in value to CHF 25.6 Billion in 2025 with volumes down 4.8% to 14.6 million watches (almost 740,000 fewer watches), a second consecutive year of moderation; the Board reports that the watch component manufacturing business for the Swiss market remained under sustained pressure, with weakness concentrated in China and Hong Kong.
- Currency volatility - Rupee weakness and Swiss Franc appreciation — The Rupee remained under pressure from a strong US Dollar, elevated US Treasury yields and portfolio outflows and is expected to trade in a broad range of Rs. 92.5-97.0 to the Dollar; the Swiss Franc appreciated over ~23% during the year, crossing Rs. 120 in January 2026, raising imported inventory costs at Ethos Limited and production costs across the Swiss value chain, and the Board lists wide fluctuations in currency among the year's challenges.
- Geopolitical conflict, tariffs and protectionism disrupting trade corridors — The Board cites geo-political tensions due to wars, tariff issues, a protectionist approach by major markets and regulatory restrictions; the US-Iran war brought additional uncertainty in the Gulf and Middle East with ripple effects in European and Asian markets, and the MD&A notes global growth moderating to 3.1% in 2026 with merchandise trade volume growth slowing to 1.9% on trade policy uncertainty.
- Input cost inflation, including precious metals and energy — Elevated gold prices increased the cost of Swiss watches; global headline inflation is projected to tick up to 4.4% in 2026, and inflationary risks from global commodity prices, energy markets and geopolitical developments continue to warrant close policy attention.
- Customer satisfaction and retention (BRSR material issue, rated a risk with negative financial implications) — Customer satisfaction directly affects reputation, customer loyalty and business growth for a watch component and precision engineering company; the Company mitigates through product quality standards, innovation, timely deliveries, competitive pricing, two-way communication channels and a customer-feedback system.
- Emissions and energy management (BRSR material issue, rated a risk with negative financial implications) — Managing emissions and energy usage is critical for manufacturing; KDDL tracks energy use and emissions through structured policies, encourages adoption of renewable energy including solar and wind, and operates emission tracking systems to monitor significant contributors.
- Water management and effluent discharge (BRSR material issue, rated a risk with negative financial implications) — The Company mitigates through effluent treatment plants (ETPs) whose treated wastewater is reused for gardening, industrial processes and production, regular monitoring of consumption, and Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems operational at three KDDL facilities.
- Occupational health and safety, and waste management at manufacturing sites (BRSR material issues, rated risks with negative financial implications) — Workplace hazards carry accident, productivity and legal-compliance exposure - mitigated via risk and hazard assessment policies, routine safety audits, health monitoring, PPE, on-site health clinics and safety training; waste is handled, stored and disposed through authorised third-party vendors with reduction and reuse to cut reliance on virgin raw materials.

business.body: KDDL Limited, formerly Kamla Dials and Devices Limited and established in 1981, is headquartered in Chandigarh and operates across India and Switzerland, serving global customers in luxury watchmaking and precision engineering. It manufactures premium watch components - dials, hands, indexes and steel bracelets - for global luxury watch brands, complemented by premium ornamental packaging for watch and jewellery brands, and a precision engineering division (Eigen) making high-precision stamped components and tooling solutions. Through subsidiary Ethos Limited it is present in luxury watch retail, and through Silvercity Brands AG it is rolling out the Favre-Leuba brand internationally.

outlook.body: Export diversification beyond Switzerland (Europe, Asia); packaging export potential to global luxury brands; electroplating in-house capacity enabling higher-value orders; Favre-Leuba brand scaling to 8,000+ watches/year by CY2026
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Stay focused and aligned on premiumisation, supplying high-value, complex-featured watch components tailored to customer requirements
- In precision engineering, build relationships with large multinational corporations and high-potential accounts in selected precision component markets, upgrade and add new technical capabilities, expand the product range and extend reach into new geographies
- In ornamental packaging, add new customers to serve leading Swiss watchmakers and others, initially for Indian requirements and then leading to global requirements
- Make manufacturing excellence a priority, focused on Guaranteed Delivery Dates (GDD), quality and Turnaround Time (TAT)
- Pursue strategic marketing initiatives, including an enhanced digital presence to showcase new products and features
- Grow precision stamping revenue through market diversification and customer acquisition, backed by a reputation for quality and technical capability
- At Pylania SA, build infrastructure and product design capabilities for the manufacture of high-end, precious stone watch dials targeted at premium Swiss watch brands
- At Estima AG, invest in strengthening the team, acquire selected machinery for high-quality and complex features and recruit skilled professionals for critical roles, supported by technical guidance from the parent company
- At Ethos Limited, shift deliberately towards the luxury and high-luxury segments, scale the certified pre-owned (CPO) business, expand the boutique network, deepen omnichannel capabilities, strengthen the after-sales service vertical and add brand partnerships, with the lifestyle vertical (Messika and Rimowa businesses) reorganised under Ethos Lifestyle Private Limited
- Use Kamla International Holdings SA as a special-purpose vehicle for strategic overseas investments
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The ornamental packaging division strengthened its capabilities during 2025-26 through the operationalisation of its Panchkula manufacturing facility, which has an installed capacity of approximately 1,00,000 premium boxes per month; capacity utilisation of this new packaging unit in Panchkula, Haryana increased during the year and the division recorded over 35% year-on-year revenue growth on rising domestic demand and a healthy pipeline of RFQs from international brands operating in India. Looking ahead, expanded capacity and the addition of new customers in ornamental packaging are projected to deliver over 25% growth in that segment, while watch component revenue is projected to improve by 10-12% on higher volumes and better realisations. Tangible fixed assets rose during the year, reflecting continued investments in manufacturing infrastructure, capacity enhancement, process improvements and technology upgrades across business segments; loan funds increased to fund capacity expansion, infrastructure development and working capital, and the debt service coverage ratio moderated on higher debt repayments and financing commitments linked to capacity expansion and infrastructure enhancement. In luxury retail, subsidiary Ethos Limited pursued an accelerated pace of boutique expansion, taking its network from 73 to 94 boutiques across 30 cities during the year (103 boutiques across 34 cities as on date), with the lifestyle vertical comprising the Messika and Rimowa businesses reorganised under Ethos Lifestyle Private Limited.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The Swiss watch industry is expected to witness gradual stabilisation through 2026 after the moderation of 2025, with recovery visible in select markets while demand in parts of Asia remains measured
- Growth is expected to be supported by continued demand in higher-value segments, with established markets such as the USA providing stability and recovery in key Asian markets an important swing factor
- India is expected to remain one of the most attractive long-term growth markets for Swiss watchmakers, supported by favourable demographics, rising discretionary incomes and the progressive reduction in import duties under TEPA
- Input cost dynamics, including precious metal prices, and currency movements are expected to continue influencing pricing and margins across the value chain
- The Indian watch industry has shifted from volume-driven sales to value-led premiumisation, catalysed by TEPA coming into force on 1st October 2025 and the resulting phased customs duty reduction on Swiss timepieces
- Organised, professionalised luxury retail - larger experiential boutiques, expansion into Tier-II cities and the rise of certified pre-owned - is expected to support demand across the broader luxury watch value chain, including premium packaging and specialised watch components
- The global metal stamping market is transitioning towards high-precision, high-complexity manufacturing driven by the pivot to EVs and miniaturisation in consumer electronics, with China Plus One, Make in India and PLI schemes adding domestic demand for Indian precision manufacturers
- The ornamental packaging market is shifting towards 'Eco-Luxury', while India emerges as an attractive manufacturing destination as global luxury brands diversify supply chains and emphasise localisation, faster turnaround and import substitution
- The domestic watch market is likely to sustain its growth trajectory, offering opportunities to increase market share, with watch component revenue improvement driven by higher volumes and improved average realisations
- At Ethos, margins were affected by the sharp appreciation of the Swiss Franc against the Rupee, which increased the cost of imported inventory, together with higher marketing investment and upfront costs of accelerated boutique expansion
- Ornamental packaging division reported a healthy pipeline of Requests for Quotations (RFQs) from international brands operating in India
- At Estima AG, management remains cautiously optimistic that an improvement in Swiss market conditions will lead to a healthier order pipeline and eventual profitability
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: KDDL delivered strong 32.5% H1FY26 revenue growth driven by Precision Engineering (44% YoY) and Packaging (70% YoY), while watch components faced global headwinds but are stabilizing; the company's vertical integration and capacity expansion in electroplating and bracelets position it to capture higher-margin opportunities as global watch demand normalizes.

open.item: Estima remains loss-making but management expects the turnaround to begin from next year (FY26) onwards.
KDDL plans to enter the watch cases business, likely in FY26 (not FY25), leveraging steel expertise from the bracelet project.
Eigen backward-integration capex (in-house plating), started last year, to be commissioned in the next 3 to 4 months, with further capacity additions; FY26 revenue ~INR200 cr (+35%).
Management expects no great change in the overall margin picture over FY27, with EBITDA/overall margins remaining in the same band (not changing dramatically up or down).
Ethos to launch a new store format this year targeting the INR25,000 to INR2 lakh price point, as it believes the wearables threat is over.
Watch components (dials/hands) expect H1 FY27 to remain relatively stable for export with growth more visible in H2; guided ~11-12% growth that could go higher if global markets improve.
Favre Leuba (present in >20 countries, >80 points of sale) expected to more than double sales in FY27 with expanded global footprint and new product launches.
Packaging division (Ornapac), currently loss-making at ramp-up, expected to become profitable during the second half of FY27.

Bracelet capacity to be expanded from the original ~75,000 to about 110,000-120,000 over the next 12 months; FY26 revenue ~INR40 cr at ~75-80% utilization, though margins may moderate near-term from lower-price-point new customers.
KDDL standalone planned capex of approximately INR50 crores across businesses (bracelet, watch components, precision engineering, packaging) during FY27, excluding subsidiary/brand investments.
Three-to-five year vision to expand into luxury segments beyond watches, including branded jewellery and other closely-related luxury categories, via omni-channel.
Ethos (having crossed 100 boutiques) targets doubling its boutique network in the next 3 years (maybe 4), per CEO Pranav Saboo.
Weak consumer demand in key luxury markets (particularly China and parts of Europe) and cautious brand inventory planning flagged as continuing near-term headwinds.
Ethos has ~7-8% of a price increase (Swiss franc-driven) still to be passed on, which management expects to improve margins as currency stabilizes without hurting volumes.
Ethos reaffirms its listing-time vision of growing 10x in 10 years, requiring ~25.9-26% CAGR, with management confident and ahead of that vision.
Bracelets and precision engineering expected to grow at about 25% CAGR medium-to-long term (packaging also ~25%); watch component a little less.
US tariffs on Swiss watches (a headwind, recently reduced from 39% to 15%) flagged as a road bump; Favre Leuba US sales expected to start delivering with lower tariffs.
Long-term business targets given in prior calls (Eigen scale, INR80-100 cr each for bracelet and packaging in 3-5 years) reaffirmed; management stands by them despite tariff noise.
After making Favre Leuba a success, KDDL will look for opportunities to acquire other watch brands across price segments, though no immediate plans.
Long-term vision to build a verticalized watch major spanning component manufacturing, watch assembly (Favre Leuba) and retailing (Ethos), similar to groups like Richemont.

verdicts.item: Management expects to maintain sustainable manufacturing EBITDA margins of 18% plus, in a broad range of 18% to 20% depending on business mix.
verdicts.note: Standalone 'for the full year, EBITDA is 23.1%' (Q4 25.1%) - above the 18-20% target.

verdicts.item: New 28,000 sq ft leased shed in Bengaluru (under development) to be operational in the second half of FY26.
verdicts.note: The new Bengaluru facility 'still under progress... in the next 3 to 4 months... will be commissioned' - later than the H2FY26 target.

verdicts.item: Precision engineering (Eigen) revenue targeted to grow from ~INR100 crores to INR500 crores, growing at a 20-25% CAGR over the next several years (not 2-3 years).
verdicts.note: Eigen 'revenue during the year is INR200 crores... growth of 35% plus'; 25% CAGR maintained - strong progress toward Rs.500 cr endpoint, not reached. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Ethos retail business targets a sustainable EBITDA margin of 10% to 11% (ex-IndAS116) over the next two to three years.
verdicts.note: expired: no update 8Q past horizon Q4FY24

verdicts.item: Silvercity Brands to globally launch the revamped Favre Leuba brand with new collections, scheduled for the last quarter of FY25.
verdicts.note: 'Favre-Leuba was already present in over 20 countries, with more than 80 points of sales. Sales is much better than expected' - global launch delivered.

verdicts.item: For the next 12 to 15 months, KDDL will focus on fully onboarding the bracelet project (with an expansion plan to be discussed) and turning around Estima before taking up other projects.
verdicts.note: Bracelet fully onboarded and profitable but Estima not addressed - focus commitment only partly evidenced.

verdicts.item: Bracelet division (commercial production started Oct 2024, INR44 cr investment, 75,000 capacity) expected to reach close to 100% capacity utilization in the next fiscal (FY26).
verdicts.note: Bracelet reached ~75-80% utilization in FY26, short of the ~100% target (capacity also being added continuously). [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Bracelet capacity to be expanded by at least 30% to 40% with balancing equipment, with continuous expansion planned over the next 2 to 3 years.
verdicts.note: 'we are continuously adding capacity... incrementally adding capability and capacity' - expansion ongoing, not a discrete completion.

verdicts.item: Secured ~30,000 sq ft leased facility in Bangalore to be operational next fiscal (FY26), with further capacity expansion via new factory construction on own land anticipated in FY27.
verdicts.note: 'Eigen capex... started last year that is still under progress. Hopefully, in the next 3 to 4 months... will be commissioned' - later than the H2FY26 target.

verdicts.item: Favre Leuba's exclusive new collection to be available internationally starting January 2025 (following the August 2024 Geneva launch), distributed exclusively in India by Ethos.
verdicts.note: Favre Leuba international distribution delivered: 'present in over 20 countries, with more than 80 points of sales'; India exclusive via Ethos.

verdicts.item: KDDL expects FY26 revenue to grow in the range of 15% to 20%, driven by watch-market recovery, precision engineering growth and higher bracelet/packaging utilization.
verdicts.note: Beat the 15-20% FY26 guidance: standalone revenue 'INR506 crores... grew by almost 31.9%' (consolidated +30.3%); 'we have done even better than expected'.

verdicts.item: Management anticipates a gradual revival in Swiss watch exports beginning in the second half of FY26.
verdicts.note: 'watch component business, dials and hands, forged a recovery during the second half of FY26' but 'Swiss watches continue to face headwinds' - KDDL recovered, broad Swiss revival muted.

risks.risk: Sustained slowdown in the Swiss watch industry, the Company's core export end-market
risks.note: Swiss watch exports declined 1.7% in value to CHF 25.6 Billion in 2025 with volumes down 4.8% to 14.6 million watches (almost 740,000 fewer watches), a second consecutive year of moderation; the Board reports that the watch component manufacturing business for the Swiss market remained under sustained pressure, with weakness concentrated in China and Hong Kong.

risks.risk: Currency volatility - Rupee weakness and Swiss Franc appreciation
risks.note: The Rupee remained under pressure from a strong US Dollar, elevated US Treasury yields and portfolio outflows and is expected to trade in a broad range of Rs. 92.5-97.0 to the Dollar; the Swiss Franc appreciated over ~23% during the year, crossing Rs. 120 in January 2026, raising imported inventory costs at Ethos Limited and production costs across the Swiss value chain, and the Board lists wide fluctuations in currency among the year's challenges.

risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict, tariffs and protectionism disrupting trade corridors
risks.note: The Board cites geo-political tensions due to wars, tariff issues, a protectionist approach by major markets and regulatory restrictions; the US-Iran war brought additional uncertainty in the Gulf and Middle East with ripple effects in European and Asian markets, and the MD&A notes global growth moderating to 3.1% in 2026 with merchandise trade volume growth slowing to 1.9% on trade policy uncertainty.

risks.risk: Input cost inflation, including precious metals and energy
risks.note: Elevated gold prices increased the cost of Swiss watches; global headline inflation is projected to tick up to 4.4% in 2026, and inflationary risks from global commodity prices, energy markets and geopolitical developments continue to warrant close policy attention.

risks.risk: Customer satisfaction and retention (BRSR material issue, rated a risk with negative financial implications)
risks.note: Customer satisfaction directly affects reputation, customer loyalty and business growth for a watch component and precision engineering company; the Company mitigates through product quality standards, innovation, timely deliveries, competitive pricing, two-way communication channels and a customer-feedback system.

risks.risk: Emissions and energy management (BRSR material issue, rated a risk with negative financial implications)
risks.note: Managing emissions and energy usage is critical for manufacturing; KDDL tracks energy use and emissions through structured policies, encourages adoption of renewable energy including solar and wind, and operates emission tracking systems to monitor significant contributors.

risks.risk: Water management and effluent discharge (BRSR material issue, rated a risk with negative financial implications)
risks.note: The Company mitigates through effluent treatment plants (ETPs) whose treated wastewater is reused for gardening, industrial processes and production, regular monitoring of consumption, and Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems operational at three KDDL facilities.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety, and waste management at manufacturing sites (BRSR material issues, rated risks with negative financial implications)
risks.note: Workplace hazards carry accident, productivity and legal-compliance exposure - mitigated via risk and hazard assessment policies, routine safety audits, health monitoring, PPE, on-site health clinics and safety training; waste is handled, stored and disposed through authorised third-party vendors with reduction and reuse to cut reliance on virgin raw materials.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The Swiss watch industry is expected to witness gradual stabilisation through 2026 after the moderation of 2025, with recovery visible in select markets while demand in parts of Asia remains measured
- Growth is expected to be supported by continued demand in higher-value segments, with established markets such as the USA providing stability and recovery in key Asian markets an important swing factor
- India is expected to remain one of the most attractive long-term growth markets for Swiss watchmakers, supported by favourable demographics, rising discretionary incomes and the progressive reduction in import duties under TEPA
- Input cost dynamics, including precious metal prices, and currency movements are expected to continue influencing pricing and margins across the value chain
- The Indian watch industry has shifted from volume-driven sales to value-led premiumisation, catalysed by TEPA coming into force on 1st October 2025 and the resulting phased customs duty reduction on Swiss timepieces
- Organised, professionalised luxury retail - larger experiential boutiques, expansion into Tier-II cities and the rise of certified pre-owned - is expected to support demand across the broader luxury watch value chain, including premium packaging and specialised watch components
- The global metal stamping market is transitioning towards high-precision, high-complexity manufacturing driven by the pivot to EVs and miniaturisation in consumer electronics, with China Plus One, Make in India and PLI schemes adding domestic demand for Indian precision manufacturers
- The ornamental packaging market is shifting towards 'Eco-Luxury', while India emerges as an attractive manufacturing destination as global luxury brands diversify supply chains and emphasise localisation, faster turnaround and import substitution
- The domestic watch market is likely to sustain its growth trajectory, offering opportunities to increase market share, with watch component revenue improvement driven by higher volumes and improved average realisations
- At Ethos, margins were affected by the sharp appreciation of the Swiss Franc against the Rupee, which increased the cost of imported inventory, together with higher marketing investment and upfront costs of accelerated boutique expansion
- Ornamental packaging division reported a healthy pipeline of Requests for Quotations (RFQs) from international brands operating in India
- At Estima AG, management remains cautiously optimistic that an improvement in Swiss market conditions will lead to a healthier order pipeline and eventual profitability

capital_allocation.body: Interim dividend: INR15/share declared; capex prioritized for capacity expansion; no M&A announced beyond Favre-Leuba; no share buybacks mentioned

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The ornamental packaging division strengthened its capabilities during 2025-26 through the operationalisation of its Panchkula manufacturing facility, which has an installed capacity of approximately 1,00,000 premium boxes per month; capacity utilisation of this new packaging unit in Panchkula, Haryana increased during the year and the division recorded over 35% year-on-year revenue growth on rising domestic demand and a healthy pipeline of RFQs from international brands operating in India. Looking ahead, expanded capacity and the addition of new customers in ornamental packaging are projected to deliver over 25% growth in that segment, while watch component revenue is projected to improve by 10-12% on higher volumes and better realisations. Tangible fixed assets rose during the year, reflecting continued investments in manufacturing infrastructure, capacity enhancement, process improvements and technology upgrades across business segments; loan funds increased to fund capacity expansion, infrastructure development and working capital, and the debt service coverage ratio moderated on higher debt repayments and financing commitments linked to capacity expansion and infrastructure enhancement. In luxury retail, subsidiary Ethos Limited pursued an accelerated pace of boutique expansion, taking its network from 73 to 94 boutiques across 30 cities during the year (103 boutiques across 34 cities as on date), with the lifestyle vertical comprising the Messika and Rimowa businesses reorganised under Ethos Lifestyle Private Limited.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and proactive; emphasized long-term growth targets, vertical integration, and resilience to short-term tariffs; highlighted execution discipline and flexibility in manufacturing; optimistic on Favre-Leuba and Precision Engineering momentum

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Long-standing customer relationships, especially with partners in the Swiss watch industry, described by the Company as a major strength on the export front
- Presence across both manufacturing and retail, enabling participation across the luxury value chain with a diversified business portfolio
- Eigen focuses on chosen segments requiring high complexity, skills and capabilities along with high entry barriers, and has moved from component supplier to strategic solution provider for global technology leaders
- Manufacturing setup equipped to handle complex export requirements, with design capabilities, fast development cycles, shortened response times and competitive pricing
- Consistent emphasis on product quality, operational agility and reliability in quality and delivery, which the Company links to tangible market share gains
- Eigen's expertise in progressive tool design and die-making, delivering high-speed, zero-defect production for complex assemblies

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: U.S. tariffs on Swiss watches (now reduced to 15%); China/HK luxury demand slowdown; currency volatility; global watch industry cyclicality; execution risk in new capacity ramp-up

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: KDDL's natural forex hedge between export-heavy KDDL and import-heavy Ethos subsidiary; precision stamping for connectors is a hidden high-margin niche supplying Amphenol/TE Connectivity; bracelet expansion uses flexible tech for small-batch production, aligning with luxury industry's shift to agility

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition/Brand] In 2023 KDDL acquired the iconic Swiss brand Favre-Leuba, with plans for a global relaunch; it is housed in Silvercity Brands AG (93.08%, directly and indirectly through subsidiaries), described as "Business of premium luxury watches under the brand 'Favre Leuba'".
- [Group vs listed entity] Consolidated figures are dominated by the retail subsidiary rather than the components business: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations is Rs 2,153.4 Cr against standalone Rs 495.8 Cr, and FY26 consolidated gross profit margin is 42.2% against standalone 74.9% — the two bases must not be read interchangeably.
- [Regulation] The FY26 consolidated P&L carries an Exceptional Expense of Rs 2.4 Cr, footnoted as "Statutory impact of Labor Codes of Rs. 2.45 Cr" (the deck states 2.4 in the table and 2.45 in the footnote).
- [Historical one-offs] FY24 standalone included an Exceptional Expense of Rs 19.6 Cr, footnoted as an "impairment allowance in the value of investment which is accounted for in other expenses"; FY23 standalone included an Exceptional Expense of Rs 19.0 Cr, footnoted as a "One-time value creation award to Mr. Yashovardhan Saboo (Chairman & MD)". These make the FY23/FY24 standalone PAT and EPS non-comparable with other years.
- [Investor relations] The deck names Sanjeev Masown as CFO of KDDL and Strategic Growth Advisors Limited as the investor-relations advisor.
